title: Part Four, Chapter 4: The Hornets and the Wasps

verses.t: And then they set out the hornets and wasps that they had gone and fetched; and when they came, they put them in four great gourds, and set all four around the town, and shut the hornets and wasps up in the gourds; and these were the ones that were to make war on the peoples. And they hid and kept watch; and the town was spied on by the scouts of the peoples. "They are not many," the spies said; and they saw only the dolls, moving their arrows and shields, and certainly they looked like killing men. And seeing them, the peoples rejoiced greatly because those they saw were not many; and the peoples were many, and the fighting and killing men who came to kill Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam, who were on the mountain Hacavitz, could not be counted. And now we shall tell how their attack went.

And Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam were there, all together on the mountain with their wives and their children, when all the enemy killers arrived. And they did not come only in a body with the peoples, but they surrounded the whole town, murmuring, armed with arrows and shields; and they shouted and whistled, and murmured noisily, and whistled through their hands. And as they came up below the town, those lords were not worried, but watched attentively from the wall, all in order with their wives and children, and waited in suspense for the outcome. And the peoples were pleased when they climbed up the mountain, and they were about to hurl themselves at the edge of the town, when those who were in the town opened all four gourds; and the hornets and wasps came out like smoke when they came out of the gourds. And the peoples perished because of the creatures, for they went straight for the pupils of their eyes, and for their noses and mouths and legs and arms. "Who will go and catch and snatch away all these hornets and wasps?" And they stung them straight in the pupils of their eyes; the little creatures swarmed and piled up on each of the soldiers, and they were as if drunk because of the hornets and wasps, and could no longer hold their arrows and shields, and these fell to the ground; and they lay stretched out on the mountain, and no longer felt the arrows that were shot at them, nor the blows of the axes; and Balam-quitzé and Balam-acab used only bare sticks. And their wives too were killers. And half of them, all the peoples, turned and ran when they saw that the first had died and been finished off; and not a few men died. And it was not those whom they pursued with all their heart who died; only the little creatures attacked them. And it was no one who made the war, neither soldiers nor arrows nor shields, when the peoples rose up and rose up in arms against Balam-quitzé, Mahucutah, Balam-acab and Yquibalam. And the peoples said, "Do not kill us, for we are poor men." "Very well," they said, "and though you deserved death, you shall only be tributaries for ever," it was said to them. And such was the subjection of all the peoples by our first fathers; and this happened on the mountain that is now called Hacavitz. And this was the first place where they were settled, and there they multiplied and increased and had sons and daughters, on the mountain Hacavitz; and they rejoiced greatly when they subjected all the peoples. And there they were subjected, on the mountain, and so it came about that the peoples were defeated; and then their hearts were at peace, and they spoke to their sons. Their death had already drawn near when the peoples wanted to kill them. And now we shall tell of the end and death of Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam.
